problem: Existing zero-shot object goal navigation methods explore inefficiently because they score semantic relevance at the object level, lacking a strategic notion of which containers or workspaces probably hold the target. Scene graph methods often depend on manually tuned parameters.
motivation: Robots in human-centric environments must find objects from natural language in unseen environments without prior knowledge. Humans search by checking likely containers such as desks or cabinets, which suggests reasoning at a workspace level rather than over individual objects.
key_idea: Dynamically build a three-layer room-workspace-object hierarchical scene graph without hand-tuned parameters, and search by scoring semantic relevance of workspaces (probable containers) instead of objects.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that evaluating relevance at the workspace level enables focused, human-like exploration and yields large SR gains.
method: Hierarchical scene graph: dynamically constructs a three-layer room-workspace-object graph, without manually pre-tuned parameters.
Workspace-based searching strategy: evaluates semantic relevance of workspaces to the target to infer probable containers and guide exploration.
results: The abstract reports SR 0.4859 under distance-constrained settings (+26.8% over the best baseline) and SR 0.7360 under unconstrained settings (+20.2%). The benchmark, split and baseline names are not given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so benchmark, baselines and implementation details are unknown.
Evaluation appears to be simulation only, according to the abstract.
